nominees.name: Chandrashekhar Joshi
nominees.affiliation: University of California, Los Angeles, USA

motivation: Tajima's 1979 proposal (with the late J. M. Dawson) showed that an intense laser pulse can drive a plasma wake with accelerating fields a thousand times stronger than conventional radio-frequency structures. Joshi pioneered the experimental demonstration of plasma-based acceleration, from beat-wave to beam-driven wakefields that doubled electron energies over under a metre. Malka led the realisation of quasi-monoenergetic, stable laser-wakefield electron beams and their use as compact sources of femtosecond X-rays and gamma rays. Together they created a new accelerator paradigm: GeV-class electrons from centimetre-scale plasmas, now used worldwide. These beams opened a new experimental frontier in fundamental physics, enabling all-optical tests of strong-field QED, including the first measurements of quantum radiation reaction. Their work connects plasma theory, laser science and particle physics, and it is the basis for proposed compact colliders and light sources.
